title: Cement, steel and engineering
author: Editorial Desk
summary: The Cement, Ispat and Engineering & Metal federations.
body:
Heavy industry has its own BMS federations: the **Akhil Bharatiya Cement Mazdoor Mahasangh**, the **Akhil Bharatiya Ispat Mazdoor Mahasangh** (steel) and the **Bharatiya Engineering & Metal Mazdoor Mahasangh**.

## Steel

Public sector steel plants, such as those of SAIL, are large employers in Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur, Bokaro and Bhadravati. Unions in the sector raise questions of **wage settlements**, **contract workers' regularisation**, **disinvestment** and **safety**. Steel is also a strategic material, and BMS argues that public sector plants should be strengthened.

## Cement

Cement is a capital-intensive industry with a large contract workforce. Workers' concerns include **bipartite wage agreements**, **dust-related health** problems and the status of contract workers in plants and mines.

## Engineering and metal

This covers a wide range of factories, from large public sector firms to small units in industrial clusters, where wages and job security vary greatly.

## The industry's common challenge

Technology has reduced the number of workers per unit of output. BMS believes that skill development and re-skilling are the practical answer, not a policy of ignoring the workers who are displaced.

The test of progress, as Thengadi Ji put it, is whether the worker shares in it.
